analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-close of an HDF5 object identifier. Reference parsing stores the dereferenced dataset ID in `matvar->internal->id`, then `Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceInfo` calls `Mat_H5ReadDatasetInfo`; when that discovers a name, `Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceInfo` closes `ref_id` because `internal->id != ref_id`, but it does not invalidate the already stored `internal->id`. Later `Mat_VarRead73`/`Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceData` treats that stale numeric ID as a live dataset ID. HDF5 can reuse the ID for another object, so the later `H5Iget_type` may succeed and `H5Dread` operates on an unrelated or invalid dataset state; in this PoV it reaches compact-dataset copying and crashes in `H5MM_memcpy`. The root cause is the premature close/stale-ID propagation in `Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceInfo`, not the memcpy helper.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A MATLAB 7.3/HDF5 file must contain a cell/structure dataset of object references. During metadata loading, a referenced dataset must have an HDF5 name, causing `Mat_H5ReadVarInfo` to populate `hdf5_name` while the caller has already saved the dereferenced handle in `internal->id`; `Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceInfo` then closes that handle without clearing it. Subsequent reference/object processing must cause the closed numeric handle to be reused or otherwise appear valid. When `Mat_VarReadDataAll` traverses the cell/structure, it passes the dangling `internal->id` to `Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceData`, which allocates from the referenced variable's metadata and calls `H5Dread` through the aliased ID. The supplied PoV's deeply nested reference graph and compact dataset produce the required reuse and invalid read.

args: In matio/src/mat73.c, analyze HDF5 identifier ownership for Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceInfo, Mat_H5ReadDatasetInfo, and later Mat_VarRead73. When a dereferenced dataset gets hdf5_name, should Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceInfo retain the live ref_id in internal->id, or close it and set internal->id=-1 so later reads reopen by name/reference? Identify the intended ownership pattern and safest minimal fix.

The reported vulnerability says callers at lines around 793 and 1034 store an H5RDEREFERENCE result into child->internal->id, then call Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceInfo. Mat_H5ReadVarInfo may populate internal->hdf5_name and apparently alter internal->id. Current Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceInfo closes ref_id whenever internal->id != ref_id, but stale state later reaches Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceData and H5Dread. I have inspected the dataset and reference-data routines: Mat_H5ReadNextReferenceData owns/closes a dataset ID after reading, while recursive cell/struct entries pass internal->id. I need determine whether metadata parsing should keep handles live for delayed data loading or close and invalidate/reopen safely, including group references.
